arxiv-2103-01460.title: Limited-Trust in Social Network Games
arxiv-2103-01460.creator: Timothy Murray, Jugal Garg, Rakesh Nagi
arxiv-2103-01460.description: Abstract We consider agents in a social network competing to be selected as partners in collaborative, mutually beneficial activities. We study this through a model in which an agent i i can initiate a limited number k i > 0 k_{i}>0 of games and selects partners from its one-hop neighborhood.

arxiv-2204-05998.title: Numerical Regge pole analysis of resonance structures in elastic, inelastic and reactive state-to-state integral cross sections
arxiv-2204-05998.creator: E. Akhmatskaya a,c , D. Sokolovski b,c , and C. Echeverría-Arrondo b
arxiv-2204-05998.description: Abstract We present a detailed description of a FORTRAN code for evaluation of the resonance contribution a Regge trajectory makes to the integral state-to-state cross section (ICS) within a specified range of energies. The contribution is evaluated with the help of the Mulholland formula [Macek et al (2004)] and its variants [Sokolovski et al (2007); Sokolovski and Akhmatskaya (2011)].

arxiv-2208-06757.title: A Preliminary Study on the Potential Usefulness of Open Domain Model for Missing Software Requirements Recommendation
arxiv-2208-06757.creator: Ziyan Zhao, Li Zhang, Xiaoli Lian
arxiv-2208-06757.description: Abstract Completeness is one of the most important attributes of software requirement specifications. Unfortunately, incompleteness is meanwhile one of the most difficult problems to detect. Some approaches have been proposed to detect missing requirements based on the requirement-oriented domain model. However, this kind of models are lacking for lots of domains.

arxiv-2306-10201.title: Stretched sinograms for limited-angle tomographic reconstruction with neural networks
arxiv-2306-10201.creator: Kyle Luther, H. Sebastian Seung
arxiv-2306-10201.description: Abstract We present a direct method for limited angle tomographic reconstruction using convolutional networks. The key to our method is to first stretch every tilt view in the direction perpendicular to the tilt axis by the secant of the tilt angle. These stretched views are then fed into a 2-D U-Net which directly outputs the 3-D reconstruction.

arxiv-2310-15078.title: Convergence of a steepest descent algorithm in shape optimisation using W 1 , ∞ W^{1,\infty} functions
arxiv-2310-15078.creator: Klaus Deckelnick, Philip J. Herbert, Michael Hinze
arxiv-2310-15078.description: Abstract Built upon previous work of the authors in Deckelnick, Herbert, and Hinze, ESAIM: COCV 28 (2022) , we present a general shape optimisation framework based on the method of mappings in the W 1 , ∞ W^{1,\infty} topology together with a suitable finite element discretisation.

arxiv-2506-09843.title: Noise in Maps of the Sun at Radio Wavelengths II: Solar Use Cases
arxiv-2506-09843.creator: T. S. Timothy Bastian \orcid 0000-0002-0713-0604, B. Bin Chen \orcid, S. Surajit Mondal \orcid 0000-0002-2325-5298, P. Pascal Saint-Hilaire \orcid
arxiv-2506-09843.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by T. S. Timothy Bastian \orcid 0000-0002-0713-0604, B. Bin Chen \orcid, S. Surajit Mondal \orcid 0000-0002-2325-5298, P. Pascal Saint-Hilaire \orcid. Noise in images of strong celestial sources at radio wavelengths using Fourier synthesis arrays can be dominated by the source itself, so-called self-noise. We outlined the theory of self-noise for strong sources in a companion paper. Here we consider the case of noise in maps of radio emission from the Sun which, as we show, is always dominated by self noise.

arxiv-2506-15644.title: Candidate Dark Galaxy-2: Validation and Analysis of an Almost Dark Galaxy in the Perseus Cluster Facilities: HST(ACS), HST(WFC3), Euclid R, Python, photoutils
arxiv-2506-15644.creator: Dayi (David) Li (李大一), Qing Liu (刘青), Gwendolyn M. Eadie, Roberto G. Abraham, Francine R. Marleau, William E. Harris, Pieter van Dokkum, Aaron J. Romanowsky, Shany Danieli, Patrick E. Brown, Alex Stringer
arxiv-2506-15644.description: Abstract Candidate Dark Galaxy-2 (CDG-2) is a potential dark galaxy consisting of four globular clusters (GCs) in the Perseus cluster, first identified in Li et al. 2025a through a sophisticated statistical method. The method searched for over-densities of GCs from a Hubble Space Telescope ( HST ) survey targeting Perseus.

arxiv-2509-12260.title: Entanglement Suppression in Quantum Field Theories: Holography, Chaos, and Mixed-State Dynamics
arxiv-2509-12260.creator: Davood Momeni
arxiv-2509-12260.description: Abstract Recent work has revealed that entanglement entropy growth in conformal field theories (CFTs) can be suppressed when a local operator quench interacts with a mixed-state excitation, providing a dual interpretation in terms of black hole scattering in AdS. This phenomenon, termed entanglement suppression , opens several promising directions for exploration.

arxiv-2602-03037.title: Device variability of Josephson junctions induced by interface roughness
arxiv-2602-03037.creator: Yu Zhu, Félix Beaudoin, Hong Guo
arxiv-2602-03037.description: Abstract As quantum processors scale to large qubit numbers, device-to-device variability emerges as a critical challenge. Superconducting qubits are commonly realized using Al/AlO x {}_{\text{x}} /Al Josephson junctions operating in the tunneling regime, where even minor variations in device geometry can lead to substantial performance fluctuations.

arxiv-2602-22098.title: Brain3D: Brain Report Automation via Inflated Vision Transformers in 3D
arxiv-2602-22098.creator: Mariano Barone a , Francesco Di Serio a , Giuseppe Riccio a , Antonio Romano a , Marco Postiglione b , Antonino Ferraro c , Vincenzo Moscato a
arxiv-2602-22098.description: Abstract Current medical vision-language models (VLMs) process volumetric brain MRI using 2D slice-based approximations, fragmenting the spatial context required for accurate neuroradiological interpretation. We developed Brain3D , a staged vision-language framework for automated radiology report generation from 3D brain tumor MRI.

pmc-12816051.title: Mediating effects of physical activity, BMI, and dietary iron intake on the relationship between depression and chronic headaches
pmc-12816051.creator: Fahimeh Alsadat Hosseini, Samaneh Bagherian, Maryam Shaygan, Cristina Cañete-Massé, Mitra Bonyani, Farid Najafi
pmc-12816051.description: Depression is a significant psychiatric condition linked to chronic headache outcomes, necessitating an exploration of the mechanisms involved in this relationship. This study aimed to examine whether physical activity, body mass index (BMI), and dietary iron intake mediate the relationship between depression and chronic headaches using path analysis. This study employed a cross-sectional approach.

pmc-12996997.title: Chronic inflammation-responsive hydrogel restores myeloid-T cell crosstalk to reinvigorate antitumor immunity against metastatic colorectal cancer
pmc-12996997.creator: Xinchao Li, Wangxian Fu, Hao Le, Rui Luo, Yingjie Li, Xiaorong Kou, Tao He, Liping Bai, Yangsong Xu, Jiayi Cao, Yixi Wang, Xinmao Yu, Peng Mi, Zichao Luo, Changyang Gong
pmc-12996997.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chronic inflammation in intermediate/advanced tumors drives burdensome protumor immune cell communication, thereby weakening immunotherapy. Conventional anti-inflammatory therapies focus on alleviating chronic inflammation whereas ignore dysfunction and scarcity of myeloid and T cells, which hinder their intercellular communication restoration. To address the dilemma, an inflammatory condition-triggered protumor inflammation-immunosurveillance shift hydrogel (TRANS) is developed to initiate adaptive immune responses mediated by intercellular communication. Triggered by inflammatory conditions, TRANS releases celecoxib (CXB) to inhibit the COX-2/PGE2 pathway, thereby reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages and mitigating protumor inflammation.

pmc-13588137.creator: Rabin DC, Masoud Mamani, Kshitis Chandra Baral, Gyu Lin Kim, Seo-Young Jo, Hyo-Kyung Han
pmc-13588137.description: Invasive fungal infections are a major global health threat, contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality, particularly in immunocompromised populations. Despite the availability of four major antifungal drug classes—azoles, polyenes, echinocandins, and flucytosine—current therapies remain constrained by dose-limiting toxicity, suboptimal pharmacokinetics, and the emergence of multidrug resistance.

pmc-13616706.title: Retinal OCTA parameters and the risk of worsening kidney function in patients with type 2 diabetes: a longitudinal cohort study
pmc-13616706.creator: Ying Huang, Gong Chen, Qianhua Fang, Zhiyun Zhao, Juan Shi, Ying Peng, Xuetong Wang, Cong Liu, Xing Wei, Lin Sun, Zhuomeng Hu, Yuening Xu, Ping Xue, Jie Hong, Weiqiong Gu, Na Li, Yifei Zhang, Xi Shen, Weiqing Wang
pmc-13616706.description: AimsTo determine whether retinal optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) parameters are associated with subsequent worsening kidney function (WKF) in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and to assess their relationship with early renal function trajectory.MethodsIn this prospective cohort study, 180 patients with T2D underwent macular OCTA imaging and were followed for renal outcomes (median follow-up, 37 months).

pmc-13645799.title: Mapping the genomic landscape of antibiotic susceptiblity in Escherichia coli
pmc-13645799.creator: Sarah Bastkowski, A. Keith Turner, Muhammad Yasir, Caroline Jarvis, Ian Charles, Mark Webber
pmc-13645799.description: Antibiotic treatment failure is frequently driven by bacterial insusceptibility, yet understanding of the full repertoire of genes contributing to this in Gram-negative bacteria remains incomplete. We used TraDIS-Xpress, a high-density transposon mutagenesis approach, to systematically define the genetic and physiological determinants of Escherichia coli K-12 susceptibility to 13 antibiotics spanning all major drug classes and multiple concentrations.

pmc-13652737.title: Genome–host association mapping reveals wheat pathogen genes involved in host specialization
pmc-13652737.creator: Cécile Lorrain, Alice Feurtey, Julien Alassimone, Bruce A McDonald
pmc-13652737.description: Plant-pathogenic microorganisms, including the wheat fungal pathogen Zymoseptoria tritici, adapt to their host environment. In plants, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been extensively used to uncover the complexity of local adaptation and disease resistance. However, the application of GWAS to decipher the mechanisms underlying fungal pathogenicity and host adaptation trails far behind.
